title: Communicating and reporting adverse events after administration
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 provides that any adverse events or reactions occurring as a result of a pharmacist or pharmacy intern administering a medication listed in the guidance should be appropriately communicated to the prescriber within 24 hours. If the adverse event includes one of the following outcomes, the event must be immediately reported to the prescriber: (i) death; (ii) a life-threatening outcome; (iii) inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization; (iv) additional treatment, testing, or monitoring in a hospital or emergency department; or (v) a persistent or significant incapacity or substantial disruption of the ability to conduct normal life functions. If the adverse event is the result of a dispensing error or is a serious adverse drug event, the pharmacist or pharmacy intern remains responsible for reporting the event to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, in accordance with Board regulations. Under Administration – Medical Emergencies, if emergency medical services are required, an adverse event must be immediately reported, as outlined in the circular's section on reporting adverse events.
exam_relevance: Tests the two tiers of communication with the prescriber, an adverse event that should be communicated within 24 hours and one that must be reported immediately because of a listed outcome or because emergency medical services were required, and that the pharmacist's or intern's responsibility to report a dispensing error or serious adverse drug event to the Board continues.

authority.name: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, March 11, 2026
authority.section: Reporting Adverse Events; Administration – Medical Emergencies, second sentence

numeric_facts.fact: time within which an adverse event or reaction should be appropriately communicated to the prescriber
numeric_facts.conditions: adverse events or reactions occurring as a result of administration of a listed medication; events with a listed outcome, or requiring emergency medical services, must be reported immediately

exceptions: An adverse event with one of the five listed outcomes must be reported to the prescriber immediately rather than communicated within 24 hours.
An adverse event requiring emergency medical services must be reported immediately.
common_confusions: Treating 24 hours as the outer limit for every adverse event, when an event with a listed outcome or one requiring emergency medical services must be reported immediately.
Treating the 24-hour communication as a must, when the circular says the adverse event should be appropriately communicated within 24 hours.
Assuming that telling the prescriber discharges the responsibility to report a dispensing error or a serious adverse drug event to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-14 in Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, dated March 11, 2026, in the Word document linked from the Department's news page on mass.gov.
